paragraphs.text: Who haply was the son of the former Gera; or the former might die soon, and this be called after his name.

paragraphs.anchor: And these are the sons of Ehud.

paragraphs.text: The governors did; but when, how, or wherefore, we find not.
Ut de haereditate singulis ante obitum prospiceret, saith Junius: that he might provide inheritances for them before his death. Abraham did the like. {Gen 25:5-6}
Where he sojourned, haply - as did Elimelech {Rth 1:1} - because of the famine.
paragraphs.anchor: And begat children in the country of Moab.

paragraphs.text: Or, After he had sent away Hushim and Basra, his wives, quas repudiavit propter causas quae tacentur, saith Vatablus.
paragraphs.anchor: After he had sent them away.
Who drove away the inhabitants of Gath.

paragraphs.text: Here we have a list of the chieftains of the Benjamites who dwelt at Jerusalem after the captivity.
Whose wife’s name was Maachah.] Who was surely an honour to her husband, with whom she is therefore once and again memorised. See 1Ch 7:15-16.

This Ner is also called Abiel. {1Sa 9:1} The Hebrews tell us that his proper name was Abiel; and that he was called Ner - that is, a lamp or torch - because he outshone others in holiness. He had another son besides Kish, the father of Saul, viz., Ner, the father of Abner. {1Sa 14:50-51}
Who was - as the Romans once said of Pompey - a most amiable son of an odious father. {a}
Alias Ishbosheth; so 1Ch 8:34. Meribbaal, alias Mephibosheth. Baal is by Hosea called "That shame."
From hence to the end of this chapter is a catalogue of Jonathan’s progeny. Of the rest of Saul’s children we read not that they had any posterity. That old verse is well known and daily verified,
“Eυσεβεων παιδεαυι τα λωια, δυαυεβεων δ ου.”
